paper.title_en: Cataclysmic Variables from XMM-Newton and eROSITA
paper.abstract_en: Cataclysmic variables (CVs) are interacting binaries where a white dwarf accretes material from a late-type donor. The most evolved systems, referred to as period-bouncers, host degenerate donors. We present XMM-Newton and eROSITA, which provide complementary views of the CV population. We summarize the capabilities of XMM-Newton for timing and spectroscopic studies, and its ability to characterize accretion geometries, magnetic field strengths, and short-term variability across magnetic/non-magnetic CVs. These data allow studies of individual systems, including magnetic period-bouncers with soft X-ray spectra and faint luminosities that offer insights into the late stages of CV evolution. We then present an overview of eROSITA as the first X-ray all-sky survey in the soft band since ROSAT, and its impact on population studies. The eRASS:4 catalog expands the known X-ray sky and will enable volume-limited samples of CVs, complete up to 500pc for standard CVs and up to 250 pc for period-bouncers. Cross-matching eROSITA detections with optical catalogs produced the largest sample of X-ray-selected CV candidates to date, that will refine X-ray diagnostic diagrams, reassess the demographics of magnetic/non-magnetic systems, and identify new highly evolved CVs. Finally, we describe ongoing searches for unknown systems, including CVs selected through probabilistic cross-matching with Gaia, and period-bouncers identified through a multi-wavelength scorecard. These efforts led to the discovery of new period-bouncers and a promising detached period-bouncer candidate, that could validate alternative models for the evolution of CVs. Together, XMM-Newton and eROSITA provide an unprecedented view into the structure, evolution, and demographics of CVs, with eROSITA laying the groundwork for future studies of compact binary evolution, the Galactic Ridge X-ray emission, and related phenomena.
